evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep says 'this could take five to ten minutes of your time. Is that okay?' — framed with time-box and implicit promise of clarity, but customer was already booked online; rep didn't ask for affirmation before proceeding to probing. Rushed past without real wait.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Rep moved directly into confirmation of address and logistics probing with no open-ended 'what are your biggest concerns' question.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — no concerns were raised by customer during the call.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: N/A — no concerns were raised, so no reflection opportunity existed.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Rep gathered property type (one-bedroom apartment), floor/stories (second floor, first floor at destination), number of rooms (one bedroom), walking distances (elevator to unit: 15–20 steps; parking to elevator: 15–20 steps), furniture (bed, sectional couch, tables, TV ~60 inches), special considerations (art piece customer may take himself, collectible cards customer may keep, TV size borderline). Box count discussed (15–25 boxes range). Destination address confirmed with unit number at both locations.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: False. Rep never asked 'Would you like us to pack your items into boxes for you?'
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: True. Rep asked: 'Normally for a one bedroom apartment we see fifteen to 25 boxes. Do you think you would follow within that range?'
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Partial. Rep provided hourly rate ($101/mover, $202 for two movers) and gave a time range (3–4 hours), calculating $606–$808 estimated cost. However, rep did not personalize this to Brendan's specific move details (prep level, stated concerns about the art piece or fragiles, etc.). It was a straight calculation without tying it back to his situation.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Full. Rep disclosed: hourly rate ($101/mover), two-mover crew, 2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute increments after minimum. No trip fee or overnight fee was applicable here, so the relevant disclosures were made. The 'not a guess' / minimum / increment framing was clear.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. After giving the estimate range ($606–$808), rep asked 'So with the estimate and the pricing Brandon, do you have questions about that?' — which is a question-check, not 'Does that feel fair?' There was no dedicated 'does that feel fair' ask, and no intentional silence held after the estimate.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: None. No mention of On-Time Guarantee or any discount terms for lateness.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: None. No mention of No Worries Damage Coverage, $2,000 coverage, no-deductible framing, or that it's built into the rate.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: False. Rep never asked 'Does that put those to rest?' or any closing check on Section 5 promises. Section 5 was entirely skipped.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Throwaway. Rep asked 'Alright, so any more questions before I let you go?' — this is the empty 'any questions?' format, not a genuine 'What's still concerning you about this move?' ask.
evidence_quotes.followup_on_remaining_concern: N/A — no concerns were raised in Section 6.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: False. Rep did not ask 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' or similar.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never. Rep never asked 'Would you like our help with your move?' or any variant. The call ended with 'Thank you so much for your time and of course, thank you for choosing Einstein' — assuming the move was already booked and simply confirming details, not asking for commitment.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: False. No mention of rate lock or that the quoted price is guaranteed.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial. Rep confirmed: move date (October 11th), pickup address (1955 Market Center Boulevard, Dallas 75207, Unit 2213), drop-off address (2808 Lackley Street, Dallas 75204, Unit 178), and two-mover crew. However, rep did NOT confirm arrival window, did NOT confirm phone number for day-of contact, and did NOT leave notes for the crew about the customer's concerns (art piece, fragile TV, etc.). Email confirmation of pricing sent, but no recap of move day logistics or crew briefing notes.

top_strength: Jeline gathered comprehensive logistics details — property specs, walking distances, furniture inventory, and special items — with methodical follow-up questions that built a clear picture of the move scope.
coaching_note: Section 2 (Their Agenda) was never asked: Jeline moved straight into logistics probing without first asking 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns about this move?' — this is the single highest-value line on the call card and it was skipped entirely, leaving the rep flying blind on what mattered most to the customer.
